title: The AI labs have a unit metric. Most engineering orgs still don’t.
summary: Anthropic's Q3 numbers put AI unit economics under the spotlight. Inside engineering orgs, the same question has a name: cost per accepted change. Here is how
body_markdown:
**Sources**


Anthropic Q3 2026 figures as reported from its October 14 investor meeting by the Financial Times and Business Insider, via[The Decoder](https://the-decoder.com/anthropics-q3-revenue-hits-16-8b-but-growth-slows-ahead-of-planned-november-ipo/) ,[Proactive Investors](https://www.proactiveinvestors.com/companies/news/1100176/anthropic-revenue-rises-to-16-8-billion-as-ipo-approaches-but-growth-slows-1100176.html) ,[Coin Insider](https://www.coininsider.org/news/anthropic-revenue-growth-slows-ahead-ipo/) and[Hugging News](https://huggingnews.com/earnings/anthropic-reports-168b-q3-revenue-as-growth-slows-from-145percent-to-45p-a19ee4ae) . These are company-presented, non-GAAP figures and may change in the IPO filing.


Bill Staples, CEO of GitLab, LinkedIn post on cost per accepted change and GitLab Duo Agent Platform Impact Analytics, October 2026.
